notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2023, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by parish school boards, which are separate governments, so they are not included. Residents also pay East Baton Rouge Parish.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.

Political money counts contributions from businesses, unions and PACs to candidates for mayor, council or board of aldermen and chief of police, e-filed with the Board of Ethics since 2023 (none were found). Candidates are matched to the office they typed when filing; reports filed on paper are not included. Louisiana allows business and union contributions. Individuals, candidates' own money, in-kind gifts, and party and candidate committees are not counted.

A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Louisiana yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
